outputs.exact_statement:
Put $$m=\binom{1200}{600},\qquad
 p=\min\{h\in\mathbb Z:h>1,\ h\mid(m!)^2+1\}.$$ Then $p$ is an odd prime. There are a specified field $K$ of order $p^4$, a specified finitely generated group $G$ containing torsion, and specified finite sums $a,b\in K[G]$ satisfying $ab=1$ and $ba\ne1$.

For $m,p$ in Theorem 1, $p>m$ is an odd prime and $-1$ is a square in $\mathbb F_p$. If $\eta$ is a nonsquare in $\mathbb F_p^*$, then $$K_0=\mathbb F_p[\xi]/(\xi^2-\eta),\qquad K=K_0[\nu]/(\nu^2-\xi)$$ are quadratic field extensions, so $|K|=p^4$.
The graph $\Gamma$ is triangle-free and has a specified fitting factorization $F_{ij}=\sum_{T\in\mathcal T}\alpha_i(T)\beta_j(T)$ over $\mathbb F_p$ with $t/m<1/100$.

There is a specified idempotent $e\in K[H]$ satisfying, for every $s\in P$, $$(u(s)-1)^\ell e=0,\qquad e(v(s)-1)^\ell=0.$$ Its regular rank $d$ satisfies $d/w>1/96$. Its coefficients are obtained by finite operations in the specified field $K$.
More than half of the $|A_0|=M^{p^3}$ characters are admissible.
For every edge $i<j$ of $\Gamma$, $e_i e_j=0$ in $K[G_0]$.

Let $\Delta$ be a finite simple triangle-free graph. For each vertex $i$, let $D_i$ be a finite group. For each edge $\gamma=\{i,j\}$, let $C_\gamma$ be a nontrivial finite cyclic group, with injective homomorphisms $\iota_{\gamma,i}:C_\gamma\to D_i$ and $\iota_{\gamma,j}:C_\gamma\to D_j$. Assume the following condition at every vertex $i$. If $1\leq k\leq3$, the edges $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_k$ are incident to $i$, and $s_a\in C_{\gamma_a}\setminus\{1\}$, then $$\label{eq:gluing-short-word}
 \iota_{\gamma_1,i}(s_1)\cdots
 \iota_{\gamma_k,i}(s_k)\neq1$$ whenever consecutive edge labels are distinct cyclically. For $k=1$ the distinctness condition is omitted; for $k\geq2$ it includes $\gamma_k\neq\gamma_1$. Then every natural homomorphism $D_i\to Q$ is injective, where $$Q=\left(*_{i\in V(\Delta)}D_i\right)
 \big/\left\langle\!\left\langle
 \iota_{\gamma,i}(s)\iota_{\gamma,j}(s)^{-1}:
 \gamma=\{i,j\},\ s\in C_\gamma
 \right\rangle\!\right\rangle.$$
Every natural map $H_i\to G_0$ is injective. In particular, the maps $K[H_i]\to K[G_0]$ induced on group algebras are injective.

Under these assumptions, there is a group $G_1$ containing $G_0$ and a central element $z\in G_1$ of order $M$ with the following property. Set $$R=K[G_1],\qquad
 f=\frac1M\sum_{k=0}^{M-1}\zeta^{-k}z^k,\qquad
 S=fR,\qquad P_i=fe_i.$$ Then $f$ is a nonzero central idempotent. There are explicitly specified matrices $$J_i\in\operatorname{Mat}_{w\times d}(S),\qquad
 Y_i\in\operatorname{Mat}_{d\times w}(S)$$ satisfying $$\label{eq:sector-rectangular}
 Y_iJ_i=fI_d,\qquad J_iY_i=P_iI_w.$$ The entries of $J_i$ and $Y_i$ lie in the group algebra of a finite subgroup of $G_1$, multiplied by $f$. Their construction uses only finite group operations and linear algebra over $K$.
For each such $\theta$, the subgroup $T_\theta$ is elementary abelian of exponent $p$ and rank at most $3$, with the trivial subgroup allowed.

Let $S$ be a nonzero unital algebra over a field $K$, and let $m,t,w,d$ be positive integers. Suppose $P_i\in S$ are idempotents and $\alpha_i(T),\beta_j(T)\in K$ satisfy $$F_{ij}=\sum_{T=1}^t\alpha_i(T)\beta_j(T),\qquad
 F_{ii}=1,\qquad F_{ij}P_iP_j=0\quad(i<j).$$ Suppose there are $J_i\in\operatorname{Mat}_{w\times d}(S)$ and $Y_i\in\operatorname{Mat}_{d\times w}(S)$ with $Y_iJ_i=I_d$, $J_iY_i=P_iI_w$. Then explicit matrices $$C_\sharp\in\operatorname{Mat}_{wt\times md}(S),\qquad
 D_\sharp\in\operatorname{Mat}_{md\times wt}(S)$$ satisfy $D_\sharp C_\sharp=I_{md}$.

Let $K$ be a field, let $M\ge2$ be invertible in $K$, and let $\zeta\in K$ have order $M$. For an integer $q\ge0$ put $Z_q=(\mathbb Z/M\mathbb Z)^q$ and $n=M^q$. There is a finite group $\Lambda$ of order $Mn^2$ and a nonzero central idempotent $f'\in K[\Lambda]$ for which explicitly specified elements $\Omega_{uv}$, $u,v\in Z_q$, form a basis of $f'K[\Lambda]$ and obey $$\Omega_{uv}\Omega_{st}=\delta_{vs}\Omega_{ut},\qquad
 \sum_u\Omega_{uu}=f'.$$ Thus $\operatorname{Mat}_n(K)\cong f'K[\Lambda]$ by its standard matrix units.

Let $\Phi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an injective ring homomorphism between unital rings, not necessarily preserving their identities, and put $g=\Phi(1_{\mathcal A})$. If $AB=1_{\mathcal A}$ and $BA\ne1_{\mathcal A}$, then $$a=1_{\mathcal B}-g+\Phi(A),\qquad
 b=1_{\mathcal B}-g+\Phi(B)$$ satisfy $ab=1_{\mathcal B}$ and $ba\ne1_{\mathcal B}$.

Under the field hypotheses of Proposition 13, suppose $A,B\in\operatorname{Mat}_r(K[L])$ for a group $L$ and an integer $r\ge1$, with $AB=I_r$ and $BA\ne I_r$. Finite formulas give a finite group $\Lambda$ and $a,b\in K[L\times\Lambda]$ with $ab=1$ and $ba\ne1$. In particular, over any fixed finite field with at least three elements, a failure of stable finiteness transfers to a scalar failure after a finite direct factor, without changing the field.

Let $k$ be a finite field, $L$ a group, and $a,b\in k[L]$ with $ab=1$. Then $T_b:k^L\to k^L$ is an injective cellular automaton, with $$\operatorname{im}T_b=\{y\in k^L:T_{ba}y=y\}.$$ For every $h$ with $(ba-1)_h\ne0$, the configuration $\delta_h$ is absent from its image.
